scenes.tts: A new question. What happens when the photoreceptors themselves die?
scenes.visual: Title card: Rods First, Then Cones. A retina strip with rods and cones side by side.
scenes.narration: A new question. What happens when the photoreceptors themselves die?

scenes.tts: In typical retinitis pigmentosa, the faulty gene is often not expressed in cones.
scenes.visual: Retina strip. The inherited variant drawn in the DNA of both rods and cones; only the rods show the gene switched on. Label: typical retinitis pigmentosa; in many forms this gene is not expressed in cones.
scenes.narration: In typical retinitis pigmentosa, the faulty gene is often not expressed in cones.

scenes.tts: Predict. If the faulty gene is not expressed in cones, should the cones be spared?
scenes.visual: Cones highlighted with a question mark.
scenes.narration: Predict. If the faulty gene is not expressed in cones, should the cones be spared?

scenes.tts: No. They die too, typically after most of the rods around them have gone.
scenes.visual: Rods fade out first; later the cones fade. Label: rods first, then cones (Xue and Cepko, 2024).
scenes.narration: No. They die too, typically after most of the rods around them have gone.

scenes.tts: Patients typically lose night vision first, then peripheral vision. Central vision goes later, when cones fail.
scenes.visual: A visual field that dims at night first, then narrows from the edges, then loses the centre. Label: Verbakel and colleagues, 2018.
scenes.narration: Patients typically lose night vision first, then peripheral vision. Central vision goes later, when cones fail.

scenes.tts: So cones depend in some way on rods. And cones carry daylight, colour and sharp central vision.
scenes.visual: An arrow from rods to cones labelled support? Three icons by the cones: sun, colour wheel, sharp letter.
scenes.narration: So cones depend in some way on rods. And cones carry daylight, colour and sharp central vision.

scenes.tts: Why cones die is not settled. One candidate is lost support from rods.
scenes.visual: Three cards appear: lost rod support, cone starvation, oxidative damage. A stamp: not settled.
scenes.narration: Why cones die is not settled. One candidate is lost support from rods.

scenes.tts: Rods make a rod-derived cone viability factor, called R D C V F.
scenes.caption: Rods make a rod-derived cone viability factor, called RdCVF.
scenes.visual: The first card enlarges. A rod releasing a small protein labelled RdCVF toward a cone.
scenes.narration: Rods make a rod-derived cone viability factor, called RdCVF.

scenes.tts: In chicken cone cultures and a mouse model, R D C V F binds basigin one. Basigin one associates with a glucose transporter, and cone glucose entry rises.
scenes.visual: Cone membrane: RdCVF on basigin-1, beside GLUT1. Glucose arrows into the cone thicken. Label: experimental models, not a human trial.
scenes.narration: In chicken cone cultures and a mouse model, RdCVF binds basigin-1. Basigin one associates with a glucose transporter, and cone glucose entry rises.
scenes.caption: In chicken cone cultures and a mouse model, RdCVF binds basigin-1. Basigin one associates with a glucose transporter, and cone glucose entry rises.

scenes.tts: Cone starvation and oxidative damage are other candidates.
scenes.visual: The other two cards brighten: cone starvation (Punzo and colleagues, 2009); oxidative damage.
scenes.narration: Cone starvation and oxidative damage are other candidates.

scenes.tts: Can vision be rescued? Gene therapy has begun to improve vision in specific genetic forms.
scenes.visual: A gene icon entering the back of an eye.
scenes.narration: Can vision be rescued? Gene therapy has begun to improve vision in specific genetic forms.

scenes.tts: One trial added a working R P E sixty-five gene. It was randomized and open-label, with masked grading of a mobility test.
scenes.caption: One trial added a working RPE65 gene. It was randomized and open-label, with masked grading of a mobility test.
scenes.visual: Trial card 1: RPE65 gene augmentation; randomized control group; open-label; masked grading; mobility course scored by light level. Russell and colleagues, 2017.
scenes.narration: One trial added a working RPE65 gene. It was randomized and open-label, with masked grading of a mobility test.

scenes.tts: At one year, treated participants did better than controls, by one point six light levels.
scenes.caption: At one year, treated participants did better than controls, by 1.6 light levels.
scenes.visual: On screen: between-group difference 1.6 light levels (95% CI 0.72 to 2.41) at one year.
scenes.narration: At one year, treated participants did better than controls, by 1.6 light levels.

scenes.tts: A later study delivered editing machinery for C E P two ninety inside the eye. It had no randomized or sham control, only the untreated fellow eye.
scenes.caption: A later study delivered editing machinery for CEP290 inside the eye. It had no randomized or sham control, only the untreated fellow eye.
scenes.visual: Trial card 2: CEP290 editing machinery delivered to the worse eye of 14 participants; single arm; untreated fellow eye; no sham control. Pierce and colleagues, 2024.
scenes.narration: A later study delivered editing machinery for CEP290 inside the eye. It had no randomized or sham control, only the untreated fellow eye.

scenes.tts: It recorded no dose-limiting toxic effects during follow-up, and signs of possible benefit.
scenes.visual: On screen: no dose-limiting toxic effects; 6 of 14 improved on cone-mediated sensitivity.
scenes.narration: It recorded no dose-limiting toxic effects during follow-up, and signs of possible benefit.

scenes.tts: The fellow eye shares the person and the testing days. But practice, expectation and fluctuation cannot be fully separated from treatment.
scenes.visual: A fellow-eye icon beside the trial; three partly faded cards: practice, expectation, fluctuation.
scenes.narration: The fellow eye shares the person and the testing days. But practice, expectation and fluctuation cannot be fully separated from treatment.

scenes.tts: The takeaway. The design limits the claim. The randomized trial supports a benefit on its mobility test. A small single arm supports observed safety and a preliminary signal.
scenes.visual: Two-row table: randomized control, open-label, masked grading: treated beat control on mobility at one year. Single arm, fellow eye only: no dose-limiting toxicity during follow-up; possible signal.
scenes.narration: The takeaway. The design limits the claim. The randomized trial supports a benefit on its mobility test. A small single arm supports observed safety and a preliminary signal.
